title: §.XIV (2): With Melanchthon hard then soft — Coena words property vs sacramental τὸ ῥητόν / Nazianzen ἀντίτυπα
pass_a_gloss: (2.) Those who with PHILIP MELANCHTHON badly informed, and pronouncing harshly concerning the Opinion of Bucer and the Helvetians in the Letter to Oecolampadius written in the Year 1522, and likewise in the Epilogue of Sentences collected from the Fathers in the Year 1530, cling too much to the property of the words of the Supper, so that they think no tropical diction underlies them — yet a diction in no way to be avoided by themselves; Nor with the same Philip better informed and having undergone second thoughts (δευτέρας φροντίδας), in the Letter to Urbanus Regius in the Year 1535 and in the Letters to Vitus Theodorus, especially that which he wrote in the Year 1543, and elsewhere passim, and also in the Letter to Johannes Crato in the year preceding his death 1559, do they contend that the letter (τὸ ῥητόν) of the words of the Supper is to be taken Sacramentally, and confess that antiquity spoke far otherwise on this matter than the more recent age, nay they remember that Nazianzen simply named them ἀντίτυπα of the body of Christ — see Pezel, Arguments & Theological Responses, Part VIII, from p. 175 to 190, and Melanchthon's Letter to Crato written in Melanchthon's Letters & Judgments part 2, pp. 384 & 385, edited by Pezel.
pass_b_english: (2.) Those who cling with the badly informed Philip Melanchthon — harsh on Bucer's and the Swiss view in the 1522 letter to Oecolampadius and in the 1530 Epilogue of Sentences from the Fathers — so tightly to the bare property of the Supper words that they deny any tropical speech in them, even though they themselves cannot avoid figurative speech on other grounds.

And they will not follow the same Philip after better information and second thoughts (δευτέρας φροντίδας): in the 1535 letter to Urbanus Rhegius, in letters to Veit Dietrich (especially 1543), elsewhere, and in the 1559 letter to Johannes Crato the year before Melanchthon's death — where he holds that the letter (τὸ ῥητόν) of the Supper words is to be taken sacramentally, admits that the ancients spoke far otherwise than recent ages, and even recalls that Nazianzen simply called them ἀντίτυπα of Christ's body.
See Pezel, Arguments & Theological Responses VIII, pp. 175–190, and Melanchthon's letter to Crato in Letters & Judgments II, pp. 384–385 (Pezel).
source_text: (2.) Qui cum PHILIPPO MELANCHTONE malè informato, & in Epistola ad Oecolampadium, Anno 1522. exarata, itemque in Epilogo Sententiarum collectarum ex Patribus, Anno 1530. de Sententia Buceri & Helvetiorum duriter pronunciante, proprietati verborum Coenae nimiùm inhaerent, ut nullam tropicam dictionem iis subesse autument, à se ipsis tamen nullâ ratione evitandam; Nec cum eodem Philippo melius informato & δευτέρας φροντίδας passo, in Epistola ad Urbanum Regium Aô. 1535. inque Epistolis ad Vitum Theodorum, maximè ea, quam Anno 1543. scripsit, & alibi passim necnon in Epistola ad Johannem Cratonem, anno mortem ejus praecedente 1559. τὸ ῥητὸν verborum Coenae Sacramentaliter accipiendum contendunt, & vetustatem longè hac de re aliter locutam fatentur, quàm recentiorem aetatem, quin Nazianzenum simpliciter ἀντίτυπα σώματος Χριστοῦ nominasse meminerunt, vid. Pezelium Argument. & Respons. Theolog. Parte VIII, a pag. 175. ad 190. & Epistolam Melanchtonis ad Cratonem scriptam in Epistolis & Judiciis Melanchtonis parte 2. p. 384. & 385. a Pezelio editis.
